- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.73) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — apply downward bias to first 5–7 forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days — apply a “cool-down” correction, reducing forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day windows: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.73 to -0.33) triggers a downward bias in forecast — reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven “rebound” after negative sentiment — if sentiment turns positive after 3 days, forecast should rise by 1–3% per day for next 3 days.
